subject: mathematics
question_text: For any x ∈ R, prove that cosh⁴x − sinh⁴x = cosh 2x.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.118, chapter 11 HYPERBOLIC FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 7. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula or definition you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Factorise the difference of squares
steps.margin_note: First mark. Read cosh⁴x − sinh⁴x as a⁴ − b⁴ and factorise. The second bracket is cosh²x − sinh²x, which is 1.
steps.memory_tip: a⁴ − b⁴ = (a² + b²)(a² − b²). Here the second bracket is the Pythagorean identity and equals 1.

recall.must_convey: That cosh⁴x − sinh⁴x is factorised as (cosh²x + sinh²x)(cosh²x − sinh²x) and the second bracket is 1.
accept: factorise as a difference of two squares and the second bracket is one
cosh squared plus sinh squared times cosh squared minus sinh squared
the second bracket is the identity cosh squared minus sinh squared equals one
difference of squares ga factorise chesi second bracket one avuthundi
split the fourth powers into squares of squares

steps.why: Expanding the exponential definitions to the fourth power is long and easy to get wrong. Factorising first removes one whole bracket at once.
common_mistakes: Substituting the exponential definitions and expanding the fourth powers.
Writing cosh²x − sinh²x as 0 instead of 1.

steps.label: Simplify to cosh 2x
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Replace sinh²x by cosh²x − 1, so the sum becomes 2cosh²x − 1, which is the double-angle form of cosh 2x.
steps.memory_tip: sinh²x = cosh²x − 1, so cosh²x + sinh²x becomes 2cosh²x − 1, and that is cosh 2x.

recall.must_convey: That sinh²x is replaced by cosh²x − 1 to give 2cosh²x − 1, which is cosh 2x.
accept: replace sinh squared by cosh squared minus one so it becomes two cosh squared minus one
two cosh squared x minus one is cosh two x
the sum of the squares is the double angle form
sinh square ni cosh square minus one ga rasi two cosh square minus one techi
the answer is cosh two x

steps.why: cosh²x + sinh²x is already cosh 2x, but writing it as 2cosh²x − 1 shows it in the form the chapter has already proved, so nothing new is assumed.
common_mistakes: Writing cosh²x + sinh²x = 1, which is the wrong sign between the squares.
Stopping at cosh²x + sinh²x without naming it cosh 2x.
